texts: On day 131 of Year 1, the wraith faded back into the water of the Sunken Cove in the morning.
Hesper refilled the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns during the following week.
The six lanterns returned to normal mist-light during the following week.

sentences: On day 131 of Year 1, the wraith faded back into the water of the Sunken Cove in the morning.
Hesper refilled the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns during the following week.
The six lanterns returned to normal mist-light during the following week.
parse: (: return_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lantern_1) (And (Member (sk_return $x) return) (Patient (sk_return $x) $x) (Past (sk_return $x)) (Member (sk_mistlight $x) mist_light) (Member (sk_mistlight $x) normal) (Experiencer (sk_mistlight $x) $x) (Member $x mist_light) (Result (sk_return $x) (sk_mistlight $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The per-member rule encodes "returned to normal mist-light" as a change-of-kind result on the lantern itself — the flat (Member $x mist_light) plus a result state typed mist_light with the lantern as Experiencer — so with (Inheritance mist_light light) it asserts each lantern IS a kind of light, rather than that each lantern resumed emitting normal mist-light.

The group-level return event (Member sk_return_1 return) (Patient sk_return_1 sk_lantern_1) (Past sk_return_1) carries no atom at all for "to normal mist-light" — no reified result state and no Result link — so what the six lanterns returned to is recoverable only from inside the distribution rule.

q2_gaps: "returned to normal <N>" — a change-of-state "to" PP whose complement names what the subject emits/produces rather than a property or kind of the subject; the State-result shape is the only licensed route and it forces a flat copular atom that mistypes the subject

directional / restitutive "back" on a motion-or-change verb ("faded back into the water") — not a Manner adverb, not clearly a verb+particle fusion (fade_back), so the instruction set gives it no slot and no explicit licence to drop it

"day 131 of Year 1" — a day-of-year index; the (Day <n>) term is defined and exemplified as the day within a stated month, and a day count with no month has no distinct term (it also cannot feed the seeded same-year-month day ordering)
review.notes: The two of-phrases ("the water of the Sunken Cove", "the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns") take the opaque Possession where the prompt's part/component test arguably yields PartOf; either reading is defensible. The BeforeBy gap for "during the following week", the six-lantern group + Cardinality + per-member "drained" rule, and the mire_essence / mist_light compound genus atoms all follow the instruction set exactly.

issues.reason: The rule's flat `(Member $x mist_light)` and `(Experiencer (sk_mistlight $x) $x)` assert each lantern IS (in the state of being) mist-light, which is false — the sentence says the lanterns returned to emitting normal mist-light, not that they are a kind of light — and *Core patterns* licenses a type atom only when the kind is readable off the words.

The half that stands: the asserted group-level `sk_return_1` carries no encoding of the stated complement, whereas *Resultatives* keeps the reified result state and its `(Result <event> <state>)` link beside the distributed flat half (the Skolem-state variant is licensed only where "the state carries its own complement per member", which it does not here); the half that does not stand: this is not an independent defect, since the rule does record the complement and a group-level result state would only replicate the mistyping confirmed in issue 0.

gaps_confirmed: "returned to normal <N>" where the complement names what the subject emits rather than a kind/property of the subject — the State-result shape is the only route and it forces a false flat copular atom on the subject

directional / restitutive "back" ("faded back into the water") — neither a `Manner` adverb, nor the `Again` presupposition tag (which presupposes a prior same-type event, not a prior location), nor a lexicalized `verb_particle` fusion; no slot exists

"day 131 of Year 1" — a day-of-year index in a `(Day <n>)` term that the instruction set defines and exemplifies as a day-of-month, so it is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month and cannot feed the seeded same-year-month day ordering
new_gaps: "during the following <unit>" is a forward time WINDOW, but the prescribed fallback when the antecedent supplies no term at that level is the point gap `(BeforeBy <ant> <new> 1 week)`, which states an exact one-week separation; there is no forward-window head (no counterpart to `WithinLast`), so "somewhere within the next week" is inexpressible
adjudication.defect_summary: For the confirmed issue the instruction set licenses NO compliant form: the change-of-kind/State-result shape is the only route for a "to"-complement change of state and it necessarily emits `(Member <lantern> mist_light)` (false), a spatial `Goal` is expressly barred for a result complement, and supplying an emit/produce event would invent a verb the text does not state — so the licensed options are to leave the complement unencoded and record the gap; on the partial, the standing half's fix would have been a group-level reified result state plus `(Result sk_return_1 <state>)` beside a per-member flat rule, which is itself blocked by the same gap.
adjudication.notes: Everything else in the parse is clean: the `Sunken Cove` name+kind split, the six-lantern group + `Cardinality` + distributed `drained` rule, the `mire_essence` / `mist_light` genus atoms, the day-part `morning`, and the `BeforeBy … 1 week` fallback all follow the instruction set. The two of-phrases taking opaque `Possession` rather than `PartOf` are defensible under the part/component test and are not a defect.
